# 1680     "# # #  📐 Log Length Distribution by Agent Type\n",
# 1681     "\n",
# 1682     "This cell visualizes the **distribution of log lengths** (measured in characters) for each agent type using kernel density estimation (KDE), giving insight into verbosity patterns across agent behavior.\n",
# 1683     "\n",
# 1684     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 1685     "\n",
# 1686     "* Creates a copy of the dataframe and calculates `log_length` as the character count of each `log` field.\n",
# 1687     "* Iterates over each `agent_type` and:\n",
# 1688     "\n",
# 1689     "  * Filters out constant-length logs (zero variance).\n",
# 1690     "  * Uses `scipy.stats.gaussian_kde` to compute a smoothed density curve.\n",
# 1691     "  * Adds a Plotly `go.Scatter` trace with:\n",
# 1692     "\n",
# 1693     "    * Shaded fill under the curve.\n",
# 1694     "    * Transparent lines for a soft visual stack.\n",
# 1695     "* Lays out the chart with clear axis labels, a white theme, and a wide format to support long-tailed distributions.\n",
# 1696     "\n",
# 1697     "# # # #  🔍 What you're observing:\n",
# 1698     "\n",
# 1699     "* Each curve represents the **distribution shape** of log lengths for a particular agent type.\n",
# 1700     "* Higher peaks = more common log lengths.\n",
# 1701     "* Narrow curves = more consistent logging behavior.\n",
# 1702     "* Flat or wide curves = high variance or occasional verbosity spikes.\n",
# 1703     "* Zero-variance agents (e.g. always emit the same log) are **excluded** for clarity.\n",
# 1704     "\n",
# 1705     "This view is especially useful when analyzing **agent verbosity**, **token consumption trends**, and **log audit patterns** across different roles in the system.\n"
# 1706    ]

# 1714    "source": [
# 1715     "import plotly.graph_objects as go\n",
# 1716     "import numpy as np\n",
# 1717     "from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde\n",
# 1718     "\n",
# 1719     "#  🧪 Prepare working copy\n",
# 1720     "df_loglen = df_agent_expanded.copy()\n",
# 1721     "df_loglen[\"log_length\"] = df_loglen[\"log\"].apply(lambda x: len(str(x)) if x else 0)\n",
# 1722     "\n",
# 1723     "#  📈 Initialize plot\n",
# 1724     "fig = go.Figure()\n",
# 1725     "\n",
# 1726     "#  📊 Add KDE for each agent type (only if variance exists)\n",
# 1727     "for agent_type in df_loglen[\"agent_type\"].dropna().unique():\n",
# 1728     "    subset = df_loglen[df_loglen[\"agent_type\"] == agent_type]\n",
# 1729     "    log_lengths = subset[\"log_length\"]\n",
# 1730     "\n",
# 1731     "    if log_lengths.nunique() <= 1:\n",
# 1732     "        continue  #  🚫 Skip zero-variance groups\n",
# 1733     "\n",
# 1734     "    kde = gaussian_kde(log_lengths)\n",
# 1735     "    x_range = np.linspace(log_lengths.min(), log_lengths.max(), 200)\n",
# 1736     "    y_vals = kde(x_range)\n",
# 1737     "\n",
# 1738     "    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(\n",
# 1739     "        x=x_range,\n",
# 1740     "        y=y_vals,\n",
# 1741     "        fill=\"tozeroy\",\n",
# 1742     "        name=str(agent_type),\n",
# 1743     "        mode=\"lines\",\n",
# 1744     "        opacity=0.5\n",
# 1745     "    ))\n",
# 1746     "\n",
# 1747     "#  🎨 Layout\n",
# 1748     "fig.update_layout(\n",
# 1749     "    title=\"Log Length KDE by Agent Type\",\n",
# 1750     "    xaxis_title=\"Log Length (chars)\",\n",
# 1751     "    yaxis_title=\"Density\",\n",
# 1752     "    template=\"plotly_white\",\n",
# 1753     "    width=1600,\n",
# 1754     "    height=550,\n",
# 1755     "    legend_title=\"Agent Type\"\n",
# 1756     ")\n",
# 1757     "\n",
# 1758     "fig.show()\n"
# 1759    ]

# 40     "\n",
# 41     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 42     "\n",
# 43     "* **Sets up the project environment:**\n",
# 44     "\n",
# 45     "  * Navigates to the root of the CodeCritic repo.\n",
# 46     "  * Adds it to the Python path so that internal imports work correctly.\n",
# 47     "\n",
# 48     "* **Loads and filters tool logs:**\n",
# 49     "\n",
# 50     "  * Reads the `provider_logs.csv` backup file from the `tests/backup/` directory.\n",
# 51     "  * Filters to include only rows where `provider_type == PROVIDER_TYPE.TOOL`.\n",
# 52     "\n",
# 53     "* **Parses and expands JSON output fields:**\n",
# 54     "\n",
# 55     "  * Safely deserializes the `output` JSON string into Python dicts.\n",
# 56     "  * Extracts individual structured fields:\n",
# 57     "\n",
# 58     "    * `return_code`, `summary`, `stderr`, `stdout`, `violations`\n",
# 59     "    * Nested `metrics`: `violation_count`, `error_count`, `files_checked`, `files_reformatted`, `lines_changed`\n",
# 60     "\n",
# 61     "* **Handles flexible field formats:**\n",
# 62     "\n",
# 63     "  * Supports both nested JSON (e.g., `metrics[\"violation_count\"]`) and flat keys (e.g., `metrics.violation_count`) in case of logging variations.\n",
# 64     "  * Ensures safe fallback behavior for missing or malformed data.\n",
# 65     "\n",
# 66     "* **Produces `df_tool_expanded`:**\n",
# 67     "\n",
# 68     "  * A clean and analysis-ready DataFrame used throughout the rest of the notebook.\n",
# 69     "\n",
# 70     "# # # #  🔍 What you're observing:\n",

# 84     "import os\n",
# 85     "import sys\n",
# 86     "import json\n",
# 87     "import pandas as pd\n",
# 88     "from pathlib import Path\n",
# 89     "\n",
# 90     "PROJECT_ROOT = Path(r\"C:\\Repos\\codecritic\").resolve()\n",
# 91     "\n",
# 92     "os.chdir(PROJECT_ROOT)  #  Change current directory\n",
# 93     "sys.path.insert(0, str(PROJECT_ROOT))  #  Ensure imports resolve correctly\n",
# 94     "\n",
# 95     "BACKUP_PATH = Path(\"tests/backup/provider_logs.csv\")\n",
# 96     "assert BACKUP_PATH.exists(), \"❌ Backup file not found\"\n",
# 97     "\n",
# 98     "df = pd.read_csv(BACKUP_PATH)\n",
# 99     "\n",
# 100     "df_tool = df[df[\"provider_type\"] == \"PROVIDER_TYPE.TOOL\"].copy()\n",
# 101     "\n",
# 102     "def safe_json_parse(val):\n",
# 103     "    try:\n",
# 104     "        return json.loads(val) if isinstance(val, str) else {}\n",
# 105     "    except Exception:\n",
# 106     "        return {}\n",
# 107     "\n",
# 108     "df_tool[\"output_parsed\"] = df_tool[\"output\"].apply(safe_json_parse)\n",
# 109     "df_tool[\"return_code\"] = df_tool[\"output_parsed\"].apply(lambda x: x.get(\"return_code\"))\n",
# 110     "df_tool[\"summary\"] = df_tool[\"output_parsed\"].apply(lambda x: x.get(\"summary\"))\n",
# 111     "df_tool[\"stderr\"] = df_tool[\"output_parsed\"].apply(lambda x: x.get(\"stderr\"))\n",
# 112     "df_tool[\"stdout\"] = df_tool[\"output_parsed\"].apply(lambda x: x.get(\"stdout\"))\n",
# 113     "df_tool[\"violations\"] = df_tool[\"output_parsed\"].apply(lambda x: x.get(\"violations\"))\n",
# 114     "\n",
# 115     "df_tool[\"violation_count\"] = df_tool[\"output_parsed\"].apply(\n",
# 116     "    lambda x: x.get(\"metrics\", {}).get(\"violation_count\") \n",
# 117     "              or x.get(\"metrics.violation_count\")\n",
# 118     ")\n",
# 119     "df_tool[\"error_count\"] = df_tool[\"output_parsed\"].apply(\n",
# 120     "    lambda x: x.get(\"metrics\", {}).get(\"error_count\") \n",
# 121     "              or x.get(\"metrics.error_count\")\n",
# 122     ")\n",
# 123     "df_tool[\"files_checked\"] = df_tool[\"output_parsed\"].apply(\n",
# 124     "    lambda x: x.get(\"metrics\", {}).get(\"files_checked\") \n",
# 125     "              or x.get(\"metrics.files_checked\")\n",
# 126     ")\n",
# 127     "df_tool[\"files_reformatted\"] = df_tool[\"output_parsed\"].apply(\n",
# 128     "    lambda x: x.get(\"metrics\", {}).get(\"files_reformatted\") \n",
# 129     "              or x.get(\"metrics.files_reformatted\")\n",
# 130     ")\n",
# 131     "df_tool[\"lines_changed\"] = df_tool[\"output_parsed\"].apply(\n",
# 132     "    lambda x: x.get(\"metrics\", {}).get(\"lines_changed\") \n",
# 133     "              or x.get(\"metrics.lines_changed\")\n",
# 134     ")\n",
# 135     "\n",
# 136     "df_tool_expanded = df_tool.drop(columns=[\"output_parsed\"])\n"

# 1139     "# # #  ⏱️ Tool Invocation Frequency (Grouped by 60-Second Intervals)\n",
# 1140     "\n",
# 1141     "This cell visualizes **how frequently each tool is invoked over time**, grouped into 60-second bins. It provides a timeline-style view of tool activity, helping identify bursts, patterns, or idle periods during execution.\n",
# 1142     "\n",
# 1143     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 1144     "\n",
# 1145     "* **Binning**:\n",
# 1146     "\n",
# 1147     "  * Floors each tool execution timestamp into 60-second intervals (`time_bin`) for time-based grouping.\n",
# 1148     "\n",
# 1149     "* **Aggregation**:\n",
# 1150     "\n",
# 1151     "  * Groups by both `tool_name` and `time_bin`, counting how many times each tool is called per interval.\n",
# 1152     "\n",
# 1153     "* **Plotting**:\n",
# 1154     "\n",
# 1155     "  * Uses a grouped bar chart to display each tool’s invocation count in each 60-second window.\n",
# 1156     "  * Bars are color-coded by tool for easy comparison.\n",
# 1157     "  * Adds numeric annotations above each bar (`text_auto=True`).\n",
# 1158     "\n",
# 1159     "# # # #  🔍 What you're observing:\n",
# 1160     "\n",
# 1161     "* This plot reveals **temporal distribution of tool usage**:\n",
# 1162     "\n",
# 1163     "  * Tools invoked in bursts will show **tall bars concentrated in narrow windows**.\n",
# 1164     "  * Regular, consistent usage will appear more evenly distributed.\n",
# 1165     "* Great for validating:\n",
# 1166     "\n",
# 1167     "  * **Concurrent execution** patterns\n",

# 3649     "\n",
# 3650     "#  Step 3: Add jitter to numeric x\n",
# 3651     "jitter_strength = 0.25\n",
# 3652     "df_tool_expanded['x_jittered'] = df_tool_expanded['x_numeric'] + np.random.uniform(-jitter_strength, jitter_strength, size=len(df_tool_expanded))\n",
# 3653     "\n",
# 3654     "#  Step 4: Create traces\n",

# 3666     "        showlegend=False\n",
# 3667     "    ))\n",

# 4744    "source": [
# 4745     "# # #  🚨 Average Violations per Tool per Run\n",
# 4746     "\n",
# 4747     "This cell computes and visualizes the **mean number of violations** generated by each tool across multiple runs, allowing for direct comparison of compliance or error rates between tools.\n",
# 4748     "\n",
# 4749     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 4750     "\n",
# 4751     "* Adds a new column `violation_count` by parsing the `violations` field:\n",
# 4752     "\n",
# 4753     "  * Supports both stringified JSON lists and raw Python lists.\n",
# 4754     "  * Falls back to zero if the field is invalid or empty.\n",
# 4755     "\n",
# 4756     "* Aggregates violations in two steps:\n",
# 4757     "\n",
# 4758     "  1. **Per run + per tool**, if `run_id` exists (more precise).\n",
# 4759     "  2. Then averages **across all runs per tool** to compute the final metric.\n",
# 4760     "\n",
# 4761     "* Constructs a Plotly bar chart with:\n",
# 4762     "\n",
# 4763     "  * One bar per tool (sorted ascending by average violation rate).\n",
# 4764     "  * Viridis-reversed color palette for visual consistency with prior plots.\n",
# 4765     "  * Labels on each bar to indicate the average number (rounded to 1 decimal).\n",
# 4766     "\n",
# 4767     "# # # #  🔍 What you're observing:\n",
# 4768     "\n",
# 4769     "* This chart shows **which tools tend to produce more violations on average**.\n",
# 4770     "* Tools at the top of the chart are more compliant or robust under test conditions.\n",
# 4771     "* Tools at the bottom may require tuning, rule refinement, or deeper inspection of common failure patterns.\n",
# 4772     "* Especially useful in QA workflows and for identifying validation targets in toolchain optimization.\n",
# 4773     "\n",
# 4774     "This view is a key diagnostic for **tool reliability and rule enforcement quality** across sessions."

# 5721     "import json\n",
# 5722     "import plotly.express as px\n",
# 5723     "import pandas as pd\n",
# 5724     "from app.enums.tool_enums import ToolProvider\n",
# 5725     "\n",
# 5726     "#  Ensure tool_name column exists\n",
# 5727     "df_tool_expanded['tool_name'] = df_tool_expanded['provider_id'].apply(ToolProvider.get_name)\n",
# 5728     "\n",
# 5729     "#  1) Compute violation count per row\n",
# 5730     "def count_violations(v):\n",
# 5731     "    try:\n",
# 5732     "        if isinstance(v, str):\n",
# 5733     "            return len(json.loads(v))\n",
# 5734     "        elif isinstance(v, list):\n",
# 5735     "            return len(v)\n",
# 5736     "    except Exception:\n",
# 5737     "        return 0\n",
# 5738     "    return 0\n",
# 5739     "\n",
# 5740     "df_tool_expanded['violation_count'] = df_tool_expanded['violations'].apply(count_violations)\n",
# 5741     "\n",
# 5742     "#  2) Compute average violations per tool per run\n",
# 5743     "if 'run_id' in df_tool_expanded.columns:\n",
# 5744     "    run_tool = (\n",
# 5745     "        df_tool_expanded\n",
# 5746     "        .groupby(['run_id', 'tool_name'])['violation_count']\n",
# 5747     "        .sum()\n",
# 5748     "        .reset_index()\n",
# 5749     "    )\n",
# 5750     "    avg_violations = (\n",
# 5751     "        run_tool\n",
# 5752     "        .groupby('tool_name')['violation_count']\n",
# 5753     "        .mean()\n",
# 5754     "        .sort_values()\n",
# 5755     "    )\n",
# 5756     "else:\n",
# 5757     "    avg_violations = (\n",
# 5758     "        df_tool_expanded\n",
# 5759     "        .groupby('tool_name')['violation_count']\n",
# 5760     "        .mean()\n",
# 5761     "        .sort_values()\n",
# 5762     "    )\n",
# 5763     "\n",
# 5764     "avg_df = avg_violations.reset_index()\n",
# 5765     "avg_df.columns = ['tool_name', 'avg_violations']\n",
# 5766     "\n",
# 5767     "#  3) Plotly bar chart\n",
# 5768     "fig = px.bar(\n",
# 5769     "    avg_df,\n",
# 5770     "    x='tool_name',\n",
# 5771     "    y='avg_violations',\n",
# 5772     "    text=avg_df['avg_violations'].round(1),\n",
# 5773     "    color='tool_name',\n",
# 5774     "    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.sequential.Viridis_r,\n",
# 5775     "    title='Average Violations per Tool per Run',\n",
# 5776     "    labels={\n",
# 5777     "        'tool_name': 'Tool Provider',\n",
# 5778     "        'avg_violations': 'Average Violation Count'\n",
# 5779     "    },\n",
# 5780     "    width=1500,\n",
# 5781     "    height=500\n",
# 5782     ")\n",
# 5783     "\n",
# 5784     "#  4) Format bars and layout\n",
# 5785     "fig.update_traces(\n",
# 5786     "    textposition='outside',\n",
# 5787     "    marker_line_color='black',\n",
# 5788     "    marker_line_width=1\n",

# 3088     "\n",
# 3089     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",

# 3092     "- **Visualizes latency cost** using a treemap, where:\n",

# 4200     "import plotly.express as px\n",
# 4201     "import pandas as pd\n",
# 4202     "\n",
# 4203     "#  Non-destructive copy\n",
# 4204     "df_treemap = df.copy()\n",
# 4205     "\n",
# 4206     "#  Truncate provider_type\n",
# 4207     "df_treemap[\"provider_label\"] = df_treemap[\"provider_type\"].astype(str).str.split(\".\").str[-1]\n",
# 4208     "df_treemap[\"source\"] = df_treemap[\"called_by_type\"].fillna(\"root\")\n",
# 4209     "df_treemap[\"target\"] = df_treemap[\"provider_label\"]  #  simplified target\n",
# 4210     "\n",
# 4211     "#  Edge list from simplified names\n",
# 4212     "edges = list(zip(df_treemap[\"source\"], df_treemap[\"target\"]))\n",
# 4213     "\n",
# 4214     "#  Recursive path builder\n",
# 4215     "def build_path(row, edges):\n",
# 4216     "    if row[\"source\"] == \"root\":\n",
# 4217     "        return [\"root\", row[\"target\"]]\n",
# 4218     "    for src, tgt in edges:\n",
# 4219     "        if tgt == row[\"source\"]:\n",
# 4220     "            return build_path({\"source\": src, \"target\": tgt}, edges) + [row[\"target\"]]\n",
# 4221     "    return [\"root\", row[\"source\"], row[\"target\"]]\n",
# 4222     "\n",
# 4223     "#  Build full hierarchical path\n",
# 4224     "df_treemap[\"call_path\"] = df_treemap.apply(lambda row: build_path(row, edges), axis=1)\n",
# 4225     "\n",
# 4226     "#  Flatten and clean hierarchy\n",
# 4227     "path_df = df_treemap[\"call_path\"].apply(pd.Series)\n",
# 4228     "path_df.columns = [f\"path_{i}\" for i in path_df.columns]\n",
# 4229     "\n",
# 4230     "#  Add final disambiguator for leaf nodes\n",
# 4231     "path_df[path_df.columns[-1]] = df_treemap.apply(\n",
# 4232     "    lambda row: f\"{row['provider_label']} (ID {row['provider_id']})\", axis=1\n",
# 4233     ")\n",
# 4234     "\n",
# 4235     "#  Ensure numeric latency\n",
# 4236     "df_treemap[\"latency_ms\"] = pd.to_numeric(df_treemap[\"latency_ms\"], errors=\"coerce\").fillna(0)\n",
# 4237     "\n",
# 4238     "#  Combine everything\n",
# 4239     "sunburst_data = pd.concat([df_treemap, path_df], axis=1)\n",
# 4240     "\n",
# 4241     "#  Plot\n",
# 4242     "fig = px.treemap(\n",
# 4243     "    sunburst_data,\n",
# 4244     "    path=path_df.columns.tolist(),\n",
# 4245     "    values=\"latency_ms\",\n",
# 4246     "    color=\"provider_label\",\n",
# 4247     "    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Safe,\n",
# 4248     "    title=\"📦 Treemap of Provider Execution Cost\"\n",
# 4249     ")\n",
# 4250     "\n",
# 4251     "fig.update_traces(root_color=\"lightblue\")\n",
# 4252     "fig.show()\n"
# 4253    ]

# 4260     "# # #  🧩 Execution Flow (Provider Type Nesting)\n",
# 4261     "\n",
# 4262     "This Sankey diagram visualizes the hierarchical execution path taken by the system during a program run.\n",
# 4263     "\n",
# 4264     "# # # #  🔍 What this code does:\n",
# 4265     "- The code groups log entries (`provider_log`) by their `called_by_type` (who invoked them) and `provider_type` (what kind of provider was called).\n",
# 4266     "- It then builds a flow network showing how control moves from one provider type to the next.\n",
# 4267     "- The width of each band represents the number of calls made along that path.\n",
# 4268     "\n",
# 4269     "# # # #  🧠 What you're seeing in the chart:\n",
# 4270     "- **Left-to-right flow** from high-level providers like `session`, `program`, and `controller`, down to mid-level like `system` and `state`, and finally to low-level workers like `agent`, `score`, and `tool`.\n",
# 4271     "- **Wider bands** indicate more frequent interactions. For example, the `state → score` and `score → tool` flows are thick, indicating heavy evaluation and tool usage.\n",
# 4272     "- **Branching paths** (e.g., from `agent` to `score`, `tool`, `agent_engine`) reveal the dependencies that agents rely on to make decisions.\n",
# 4273     "\n",
# 4274     "This diagram is useful for identifying:\n",

# 5125     "import plotly.graph_objects as go\n",
# 5126     "\n",
# 5127     "#  Step 1: Clean copy\n",
# 5128     "df_sankey = df.copy()\n",
# 5129     "\n",
# 5130     "#  Step 2: Simplify labels to suffix\n",
# 5131     "df_sankey[\"source\"] = df_sankey[\"called_by_type\"].fillna(\"start\")\n",
# 5132     "df_sankey[\"target\"] = df_sankey[\"provider_type\"]\n",
# 5133     "df_sankey[\"source_label\"] = df_sankey[\"source\"].apply(lambda x: str(x).split(\".\")[-1])\n",
# 5134     "df_sankey[\"target_label\"] = df_sankey[\"target\"].apply(lambda x: str(x).split(\".\")[-1])\n",
# 5135     "\n",
# 5136     "#  Step 3: Enforce node order by appearance in time\n",
# 5137     "ordered_labels = pd.concat([df_sankey[\"source_label\"], df_sankey[\"target_label\"]], ignore_index=True).dropna().unique().tolist()\n",
# 5138     "node_indices = {label: i for i, label in enumerate(ordered_labels)}\n",
# 5139     "\n",
# 5140     "#  Step 4: Build link data\n",
# 5141     "link_data = (\n",
# 5142     "    df_sankey.groupby([\"source_label\", \"target_label\"])\n",
# 5143     "    .size()\n",
# 5144     "    .reset_index(name=\"count\")\n",
# 5145     "    .assign(\n",
# 5146     "        source_idx=lambda d: d[\"source_label\"].map(node_indices),\n",
# 5147     "        target_idx=lambda d: d[\"target_label\"].map(node_indices)\n",
# 5148     "    )\n",
# 5149     ")\n",
# 5150     "\n",
# 5151     "#  Step 5: Plot Sankey\n",
# 5152     "fig = go.Figure(go.Sankey(\n",
# 5153     "    node=dict(\n",
# 5154     "        pad=15,\n",
# 5155     "        thickness=20,\n",
# 5156     "        line=dict(color=\"black\", width=0.5),\n",
# 5157     "        label=ordered_labels\n",
# 5158     "    ),\n",
# 5159     "    link=dict(\n",
# 5160     "        source=link_data[\"source_idx\"],\n",
# 5161     "        target=link_data[\"target_idx\"],\n",
# 5162     "        value=link_data[\"count\"]\n",
# 5163     "    )\n",
# 5164     "))\n",
# 5165     "\n",
# 5166     "fig.update_layout(title_text=\"🧩 Execution Flow\", font_size=14)\n",

# 9296     "import plotly.express as px\n",
# 9297     "\n",
# 9298     "#  Work on a copy to avoid modifying the original DataFrame\n",
# 9299     "df_latency = df.copy()\n",
# 9300     "\n",
# 9301     "#  Truncate provider_type to the part after the last '.'\n",
# 9302     "df_latency['provider_type'] = df_latency['provider_type'].apply(lambda x: x.split('.')[-1])\n",
# 9303     "\n",
# 9304     "#  Sum latency by provider type\n",
# 9305     "latency_by_type = (\n",
# 9306     "    df_latency.groupby(\"provider_type\")[\"latency_ms\"]\n",
# 9307     "    .sum()\n",
# 9308     "    .reset_index()\n",
# 9309     "    .sort_values(\"latency_ms\", ascending=False)\n",
# 9310     ")\n",
# 9311     "\n",
# 9312     "#  Plot as bar chart\n",
# 9313     "fig = px.bar(\n",
# 9314     "    latency_by_type,\n",
# 9315     "    x=\"provider_type\",\n",
# 9316     "    y=\"latency_ms\",\n",
# 9317     "    text=\"latency_ms\",\n",
# 9318     "    title=\"⏱️ Total Latency by Provider Type\",\n",
# 9319     "    labels={\"provider_type\": \"Provider Type\", \"latency_ms\": \"Total Latency (ms)\"},\n",
# 9320     "    color=\"provider_type\",\n",

# 9322     ")\n",

# 10501     "\n",

# 866     "\n",

# 874     "\n",
# 875     "  * Solid arrows represent sequential transitions with labeled metadata (e.g., `ACCEPTED | AGENT`).\n",

# 877     "\n",

# 879     "\n",
# 880     "  * Background colors are applied per provider type (e.g., AGENT = pink, SYSTEM = yellow).\n",

# 1229     "# # #  🔢 State Transition Frequency Matrix\n",
# 1230     "\n",
# 1231     "This code generates a **heatmap** to visualize the frequency of transitions between FSM states, using a cross-tabulated matrix of `from_state` → `to_state` transitions.\n",
# 1232     "\n",
# 1233     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 1234     "\n",
# 1235     "* **Prepares the data**:\n",
# 1236     "\n",
# 1237     "  * Uses `groupby` and `unstack` to build a **2D matrix** of transition counts between states, where rows are `from_state` and columns are `to_state`.\n",
# 1238     "  * Missing transitions are filled with 0 for clarity.\n",
# 1239     "\n",
# 1240     "* **Creates a heatmap**:\n",
# 1241     "\n",
# 1242     "  * Uses `seaborn.heatmap` to visualize the matrix with:\n",
# 1243     "\n",
# 1244     "    * Cell annotations (`annot=True`) showing the exact count.\n",
# 1245     "    * A **`PuBuGn`** color palette for smooth, visually appealing gradients.\n",
# 1246     "    * Gridlines and light styling to improve readability.\n",
# 1247     "\n",
# 1248     "* **Enhances visual formatting**:\n",
# 1249     "\n",
# 1250     "  * Axis labels are rotated and resized for clarity.\n",
# 1251     "  * A color bar (`cbar_kws`) provides a visual key for interpreting transition volume.\n",
# 1252     "  * Spacing and padding are adjusted for professional appearance.\n",
# 1253     "\n",
# 1254     "# # # #  🔍 What you're observing:\n",
# 1255     "\n",
# 1256     "* A **heatmap** showing how often each FSM state transitions to another.\n",
# 1257     "* The **x-axis** represents destination states (`to_state`), while the **y-axis** represents source states (`from_state`).\n",
# 1258     "* Darker or more saturated cells indicate **higher frequency transitions**.\n",
# 1259     "* This matrix helps identify:\n",
# 1260     "\n",
# 1261     "  * **Dominant paths** through the FSM\n",
# 1262     "  * **Rare or unexpected transitions**\n",
# 1263     "  * Potential **bottlenecks or dead ends** in execution flow\n",
# 1264     "\n",
# 1265     "This visualization is ideal for **summarizing system-wide behavior**, especially when analyzing multiple FSM runs or diagnosing state machine complexity.\n"

# 1286     "import seaborn as sns\n",
# 1287     "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
# 1288     "\n",
# 1289     "df_vis1 = df.copy()\n",
# 1290     "\n",
# 1291     "#  Build transition frequency matrix\n",
# 1292     "transition_counts = (\n",
# 1293     "    df_vis1\n",
# 1294     "    .groupby(['from_state', 'to_state'])\n",

# 1305     "    transition_counts,\n",
# 1306     "    annot=True,\n",
# 1307     "    fmt=\"d\",\n",
# 1308     "    cmap=\"PuBuGn\",\n",
